output.off_hire_clause: Off hire (fictional, modelled on NYPE 1993 clause 17): in the event of loss of time from breakdown of, or damage to, hull, machinery or equipment, or any other similar cause preventing the full working of the vessel, the payment of hire shall cease for the time thereby lost. All bunkers used by the vessel while off hire shall be for the owners' account. Rider (fictional): in the event of a breakdown of the vessel's cargo cranes, hire shall be reduced pro rata for the time lost, in the proportion that the number of cranes out of use bears to the total number of cranes.
output.war_risks_clause: War risks (fictional, modelled on BIMCO CONWARTIME 2013): the vessel shall not be obliged to proceed through any area where, in the reasonable judgement of the Master and/or the owners, she may be exposed to war risks. If the owners so decide, the charterers shall give other orders, and the vessel shall proceed by an alternative route. Extra time and bunkers on that route are for the charterers' account.

result.result:
The Master’s report shows crane No. 1 failed at Santos at 1030 UTC on 22 Jan 2025 and was repaired by 1650 UTC; loading at hold 1 stopped in the meantime, so the breakdown prevented full working of the vessel under the CP’s off-hire clause, and the crane rider cuts hire pro rata — one of four cranes out for 6.33 hours (0.066 days, 25% share). The voyage management system’s simulated hire statement figures: hire deducted US$791.67 at US$12,000 per day, no bunkers reported used while off hire (these are made-up simulation figures). It is the operator’s decision whether to put the ship off hire pro rata and notify the owner. On a yes: (a) a voyage management system entry for the off-hire period 2025-01-22T10:30:00Z to 2025-01-22T16:50:00Z with cranes_out = 1, and (b) an e-mail to the owner’s vessel technical management giving the period, crane No. 1 and the reason. Nothing should be sent or entered until the operator answers.

The port call itself is not affected: this was only a loading interruption at Santos, not a change to arrival, speed or ETA notice timing.

draft.subject: MV CALDER SOUND (SIM-0120) - Off-hire notice: crane No. 1 failure at Santos, 22 Jan 2025
draft.body:
Dear Owner,

This email concerns MV CALDER SOUND (SIM-0120).

Following the Master's report, crane No. 1 failed at Santos port with an electrical fault in the slewing motor at 1030 UTC on 22 Jan 2025, and loading at hold 1 stopped. The fault was repaired by the ship's electrician and the crane was back at work at 1650 UTC.

The operator has agreed to put the vessel off hire pro rata for the period 2025-01-22T10:30:00Z to 2025-01-22T16:50:00Z (6.33 hours), one of four cranes out of use.

Hire deducted: US$791.67 at US$12,000 per day (simulated figures).

No bunkers were used while off hire.

Please confirm the off-hire.

Regards,
Operations
